newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy bankers don't see BOI cutting rates until 97.
newsitem.headline: Italy bankers don't see BOI cutting rates until 97.

text.p: The Bank of Italy will not cut its key discount rate further this year but will reduce it by one percentage point to 6.5 percent in 1997, the Italian banking association ABI said in its annual financial outlook.
Next year's cut will come despite inflation expected to stay at around 3.0 percent for the whole of the year, ABI said.
ABI forecast GDP growth of 0.8 percent for 1996 and of 1.2 percent next year, with the lira steady around 1,000 per mark and at 1,532 per dollar next year.
After the central bank's 75 basis point rate cut to 7.5 percent on October 23, the discount rate "is expected to remain unchanged in the last two months of 1996," ABI said.
A further cut of one percentage point is expected "only during the course of 1997," its outlook added.
ABI said the Bank of Italy's expected rigour was directly linked to its anti-inflation stance and meant to ensure greater lira stability ahead of the currency's return to the European currency grid.
Next year's rate cut could take place even in a situation of "substantial stability" in inflation which ABI saw at an average 3.0 percent in 1997, unchanged from a year-on-year rate at end-1997.
Faced with a higher than expected inflation rate, however, the central bank could tighten its monetary policy stance, the outlook said. -- Rome newsroom +392 66129589
